   307	# --- one trial (runs in a background job; writes its row to $JOBS_DIR/<id>.row)

   309	  local ws="$1" out="$1/.eval/agent-output.json" err="$1/.eval/agent-stderr.log" rc
   310	  rc="$(jq -r '.exit_code // 0' "$ws/.eval/executor.json" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
   311	  case "$rc" in 124|137|143) return 0 ;; esac
   312	  [[ "$(jq -r '.subtype // ""' "$out" 2>/dev/null)" == "missing" ]] && return 0
   313	  [[ -n "$(jq -r '.api_error_status // empty' "$out" 2>/dev/null)" ]] && return 0

   319	run_trial() {  # run_trial <job-id> <arm> <fixture> <trial>
   320	  local jid="$1" arm="$2" fx="$3" trial="$4"

   324	  local start_ms end_ms per_trial ex_rc
   325	  per_trial="$(yq -r '.timeout.per_trial // 1500' "$task")"
   326	  start_ms="$(date +%s%N | cut -c1-13)"
   327	  if ! verify_corpus "$fx" >"$JOBS_DIR/$jid.digest" 2>"$JOBS_DIR/$jid.drift"; then
   328	    printf 'DRIFT\n' > "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.flag"; return 0
   329	  fi
   330	  while [[ $attempt -lt 2 ]]; do
   331	    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
   332	    trial_id="$run_id-$arm-$fx-t$trial-a$attempt-$jid"
   333	    ws="$("$SCRIPT_DIR/sandbox.sh" create --fixture "review-prs/$fx" --run-id "$run_id" --trial-id "$trial_id" 2>/dev/null)" \
   334	      || { err_json='{"type":"infrastructure_error","message":"sandbox creation failed"}'; break; }
   335	    ex_rc=0
   336	    EVAL_PROMPT_TREE="$WORKTREE" EVAL_MODEL="$MODEL" LOA_EVAL_ARM="$arm" LOA_EVAL_SUITE_FILE="$SUITE_FILE" \
   337	      LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT="$SRC_FULL" LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1 \
   338	      "$SCRIPT_DIR/execute-agent.sh" --task-yaml "$task" --workspace "$ws" \
   339	        --run-id "$run_id" --trial-id "$trial_id" --timeout "$per_trial" \
   340	        >/dev/null 2>"$JOBS_DIR/$jid.exec.log" || ex_rc=$?
   341	    [[ -f "$ws/.eval/executor.json" ]] && executor="$(cat "$ws/.eval/executor.json")"

   343	      local gout gexit=0

   345	        --timeout "$(yq -r '.timeout.per_grader // 60' "$task")" 2>/dev/null)" || gexit=$?

   353	    if [[ $ex_rc -eq 1 ]] && is_transport_failure "$ws"; then
   354	      err_json="$(jq -cn --argjson a "$attempt" '{type:"transport_error",message:"executor transport failure",attempt:$a}')"

   360	      fi
   361	    else

   363	    fi

   365	  done
   366	  end_ms="$(date +%s%N | cut -c1-13)"

   369	    "$SCRIPT_DIR/sandbox.sh" destroy --trial-id "$trial_id" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
   370	  fi
   371	  jq -cn --arg run_id "$run_id" --arg batch "$BATCH" --arg suite "$SUITE" --arg task_id "$task_id" \
   372	    --arg fixture "$fx" --arg arm "$arm" --argjson trial "$trial" --argjson attempts "$attempt" \
   373	    --arg status "$status" --arg ts "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" --arg run_date "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)" \
   374	    --argjson duration_ms "$(( end_ms - start_ms ))" --arg src "$SRC_FULL" --arg model_req "$MODEL" \
   375	    --argjson executor "$executor" --argjson graders "$graders" --argjson composite "$composite" \
   376	    --argjson error "$err_json" --arg digest "$CORPUS_DIGEST" --arg digest_now "$(cat "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.digest" 2>/dev/null)" \

   378	      arm: $arm, trial: $trial, attempts: $attempts, status: $status, timestamp: $ts, run_date: $run_date,
   379	      duration_ms: $duration_ms, source_commit: $src, model_requested: $model_req,
   380	      model_id: ($executor.model_id? // null), model_version: ($executor.model_id? // "none"), seed: null,
   381	      corpus_sha256: $digest, corpus_sha256_at_trial: $digest_now, fixture_verified: true, graders: $graders, composite: $composite, error: $error}
   382	     + (if $executor == null then {} else {executor: $executor} end)' > "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row.tmp"
   383	  mv "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row.tmp" "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row"
   384	}

   386	keep_artifacts() {  # keep_artifacts <ws> <arm> <task_id> <trial> <suffix>
   387	  local ws="$1" dest="$BATCH_DIR/$2/artifacts/$3/trial-$4$5" f
   388	  mkdir -p "$dest"

   396	}
   397	
   398	# Parent-side: append a finished job's row and update the counters.
   399	collect() {  # collect <job-id> <arm>
   400	  local jid="$1" arm="$2" i
   401	  i="$(arm_index "$arm")"

   407	    mkdir -p "$BATCH_DIR/$arm"

   409	    if [[ "$(jq -r '.status' "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row")" == "completed" ]]; then
   410	      DONE[$i]=$(( ${DONE[$i]} + 1 ))
   411	      log "done $jid ($(jq -r '"\(.arm) \(.fixture) t\(.trial) recall=\(([.graders[]? | select(.name=="recall-vs-defects.sh") | .details.recall][0]) // "n/a") \(.duration_ms/1000|floor)s"' "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row"))"
   412	    else
   413	      FAILED[$i]=$(( ${FAILED[$i]} + 1 ))
   414	      log "FAILED $jid ($(jq -c '.error' "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row"))"
   415	    fi
   416	    rm -f "$JOBS_DIR/$jid".*
   417	  else
   418	    FAILED[$i]=$(( ${FAILED[$i]} + 1 ))
   419	    log "FAILED $jid (no row written; see $JOBS_DIR/$jid.exec.log)"
   420	  fi
   421	  write_status
   422	}
   423	
   424	log "start suite=$SUITE batch=$BATCH source=$SRC12 model=$MODEL trials=${#PLAN[@]} concurrency=$CONCURRENCY worktree=$WORKTREE"
   425	write_status
   426	trap 'log "interrupted"; set_state failed; exit 3' INT TERM HUP
   427	
   428	PIDS=() PJOB=() PARM=()
   429	reap() {  # reap until fewer than $1 jobs run
   430	  local i
   431	  while [[ ${#PIDS[@]} -ge $1 ]]; do
   432	    for i in "${!PIDS[@]}"; do
   433	      if ! kill -0 "${PIDS[$i]}" 2>/dev/null; then
   434	        wait "${PIDS[$i]}" 2>/dev/null || true
   435	        collect "${PJOB[$i]}" "${PARM[$i]}"

   437	        PIDS=("${PIDS[@]+"${PIDS[@]}"}"); PJOB=("${PJOB[@]+"${PJOB[@]}"}"); PARM=("${PARM[@]+"${PARM[@]}"}")
   438	        break
   439	      fi
   440	    done
   441	    [[ ${#PIDS[@]} -ge $1 ]] && sleep 1
   442	  done
   443	  return 0
   444	}
   445	
   446	n=0
   447	for p in "${PLAN[@]}"; do
   448	  IFS='|' read -r a f t <<<"$p"
   449	  n=$((n + 1)); jid="$(printf 'j%04d' "$n")"
   450	  reap "$CONCURRENCY"
   451	  run_trial "$jid" "$a" "$f" "$t" &
   452	  PIDS+=("$!"); PJOB+=("$jid"); PARM+=("$a")
   453	done

   455	
   456	total_done=0 total_failed=0

   461	  set_state failed; log "failed: no trial completed ($total_failed failed)"; exit 3
   462	else
   463	  set_state partial; log "partial: $total_done done, $total_failed failed"; exit 1
   464	fi

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator
commands.description: Author or improve the run-<unit> skill - a per-project skill that tells agents how to build, launch, and drive this project's app. Use when the user asks to set up the project, get it running, write run instructions, or verify build/run steps work from a clean environment.

commands.name: plugin-authoring
commands.description: Make a mod: a change to Claude's own interface or behaviour, such as a live pane or panel, a band above the prompt, a status line, a toast, a slash command, or a hook on tool calls or prompts. Use to make, change or debug a mod or its hooks module.

commands.name: implement
commands.description: Execute sprint tasks with production-quality code and tests (from pr/head/.claude/skills — applies when working on files under pr/head/) (project)

commands.name: review-sprint
commands.description: Validate sprint implementation against acceptance criteria (from pr/head/.claude/skills — applies when working on files under pr/head/) (project)

Replays are 29 # excluded and counted: replay == true (LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1 at the source), or, 30 # for rows that predate the flag, a cwd under ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ or containing 31 # /bats-run-, /bats., /evals/results/ or /sandbox/, or a UTC minute holding 32 # BURST_ROWS (10) or more block rows (a suite replaying fixtures into the live 33 # log from inside the repository; no interactive session blocks ten commands in 34 # one minute). A block is a likely false 35 # positive (a heuristic) when its command holds a heredoc (`<<`; or, when 36 # .claude/scripts/lib/heredoc-classifier.sh defines heredoc_nonexec, a heredoc 37 # that function calls non-executing), when its cwd lies outside the repository 38 # (this checkout and its main worktree), or when its pattern id is a prose class 39 # (SP-1, FR-MERGE-2, FR-2-AMBIGUOUS) with no destructive verb at statement start. 40 # A real catch is a block that is not a likely false positive. 41 # 42 # Privacy: no command text, cwd, hostname, user or model name is written to any 43 # output; ids match ^[A-Za-z0-9._/:-]+$; origin text comes from the tracked map. 44 # 45 # Usage: 46 # guard-yield.sh [--window-days 30] [--audit-log PATH] [--origins PATH] 47 # [--floor PATH] [--out grimoires/loa/guards.md] [--yield-dir .run] 48 # [--hooks-table] [--check] [--json] [--root DIR] 49 # [--settings PATH] [--fence PATH] [--validator PATH] 50 # [--hooks-ref PATH] [--now YYYY-MM-DD|YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ|EPOCH] 51 # 52 # Exit codes: 53 # 0 written, or in sync (--check) 54 # 1 drift (--check): guards.md or the hooks table differ from what would be written 55 # 2 usage error 56 # 3 unreadable or unparseable input (a missing audit log is a WARN and an empty yield) 57 # 5 a guard without an origin row, a row that resolves to nothing, an invalid row, 58 # a floor mismatch, or a hook command outside the canonical schema 59 # 60 # Tested by tests/unit/guard-yield.bats and tests/unit/guard-origins.bats. 61 # ============================================================================= 62 set -euo pipefail 63 export LC_ALL=C 64 65 SCRIPT_NAME="guard-yield.sh" 66 SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd -P)" 67 68 usage() { 69 sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Tested/p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed -e 's/^# \{0,1\}//' -e '/^Tested/d' 70 } 71 die() { local code="$1"; shift; echo "$SCRIPT_NAME: $*" >&2; exit "$code"; } 72 warn() { echo "$SCRIPT_NAME: WARN: $*" >&2; } 73 74 ROOT="" WINDOW_DAYS=30 AUDIT_LOG="" ORIGINS="" FLOOR="" OUT="" YIELD_DIR="" HOOKS_REF="" 75 SETTINGS="" FENCE="" VALIDATOR="" NOW="" 76 DO_HOOKS_TABLE=0 DO_CHECK=0 DO_JSON=0 77 78 need_arg() { [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die 2 "$1 needs a value (see --help)"; } 79 while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do 80 case "$1" in 81 --window-days) need_arg "$@"; WINDOW_DAYS="$2"; shift 2 ;; 82 --audit-log) need_arg "$@"; AUDIT_LOG="$2"; shift 2 ;; 83 --origins) need_arg "$@"; ORIGINS="$2"; shift 2 ;; 84 --floor) need_arg "$@"; FLOOR="$2"; shift 2 ;; 85 --out) need_arg "$@"; OUT="$2"; shift 2 ;; 86 --yield-dir) need_arg "$@"; YIELD_DIR="$2"; shift 2 ;; 87 --root) need_arg "$@"; ROOT="$2"; #!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# guard-yield.sh — the guard register and its 30-day host yield (cycle-129 FR-1)
# =============================================================================
# Enumerates every guard Loa ships and joins it with its origin and its yield:
#   hooks       every command registered in .claude/settings.json, parsed against
#               the canonical schema "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"/.claude/<path> [args]
#               (or the same wrapped in hook-guard.sh); one row per unique script
#   fences      the `# @guard fence:<id>` markers in block-destructive-bash.sh,
#               cross-checked both ways against its emit_block call sites and
#               its literal `pattern_id: "<id>"` audit constants
#   validators  the `# @guard validator:<id>` markers in validate-artifact.sh
#   gates       the fixed list in the origin map (each row's `script` must exist)
#   policies    the floor policies in the origin map
# Origins, class, status, knob and floor come from .claude/data/guard-origins.yaml;
# the floor set must equal .claude/data/floor.yaml floor_guards.
#
# Outputs:
#   grimoires/loa/guards.md        tracked, STRUCTURAL ONLY (a pure function of the
#                                  repository; no timestamp, no yield) — --check gates it
#   .run/guard-yield.md, .json     untracked host yield: blocks_30d, likely_fp_30d,

 # Skill Frontmatter Invariants
 
 SKILL.md frontmatter keys interact across two permission layers: the skill's own `capabilities` / `allowed-tools` declarations, and Claude Code's per-agent-type tool allowlist. # Skill Frontmatter Invariants

SKILL.md frontmatter keys interact across two permission layers: the skill's own `capabilities` / `allowed-tools` declarations, and Claude Code's per-agent-type tool allowlist. When the two disagree, the agent-type allowlist wins — silently. Agents that declare write capability but dispatch through a read-only agent type produce correct output and then refuse to persist it.

## The invariant

When a skill declares write capability — either `capabilities.write_files: true` OR `allowed-tools` listing `Write`/`Edit` — it MUST NOT set `agent:` to a type that excludes those tools.

Allowed: omit the `agent:` key (skill runs in the caller's context), or set `agent:` to a write-capable type (`general-purpose`, `claude`, `fork`).

## Agent type tool allowlists

| Agent type | Write / Edit / NotebookEdit | Use for |
|------------|-----------------------------|---------|
| `general-purpose`, `claude`, `fork` | ✓ all tools | Skills that author files |
| `Plan` | ✗ excluded | Read-only planning / exploration |
| `Explore` | ✗ excluded | Read-only codebase analysis |
| `loa-scout`, `prompt-auditor`, `prompt-auditor-io` | ✗ excluded | Read-only project agents (`.claude/agents/`) |
| (unset) | inherited from caller | Default; safe for write-capable skills |

Source: Claude Code agent-type definitions in the system prompt, and `.claude/agents/*.md`.

## Enforcement

`.claude/scripts/validate-skill-capabilities.sh` checks this invariant on every SKILL.md. A violation exits with code 1 and message:

> agent type '<name>' excludes Write/Edit tools but skill declares write capability …

The allowlist is maintained in `.claude/data/agent-types.yaml` (one `write_capable` flag per agent type); the script loads the `true` entries into `WRITE_CAPABLE_AGENTS` and falls back to `general-purpose` alone when the file is missing, unparsable, or lists no `write_capable: true` entry. Adding a new write-capable agent type is intentionally a one-line edit with reviewer visibility.

## Mechanical C-PROC-001 enforcement via `disallowed-tools` (cycle-114 FR-4)

`disallowed-tools` frontmatter (Claude Code ≥2.1.152) removes tools from the
model while a skill is active — a harness-level barrier that instructions
cannot override. Cycle-114 uses it to make C-PROC-001 ("NEVER write application
code outside `/implement`") mechanical for review skills rather than prose-only.

| Skill class | `disallowed-tools` | Why |
|-------------|--------------------|-----|
| Pure-review (`write_files: false`, no report artifacts) | `Write`, `Edit`, `NotebookEdit` | Never writes anything — remove the write tools outright |
| Sprint review/audit (`reviewing-code`, `auditing-security`; `write_files: true`) | `NotebookEdit` | Write STATE-zone feedback/checkmarks/COMPLETED markers, run the allowed verdict check and run `adversarial-review.sh` (forks the provider CLIs, appends the `.run` cost and MODELINV ledgers, moves the previous round's a2a envelope aside as `.prev`, writes the new one; review also runs `qmd-context-query.sh`); System remains `none` and App remains `read` |
| Report-authoring review (`red-teaming`, `bridgebuilder-review`; `write_files: true`) | `NotebookEdit`, `Bash(git add/commit/push *)` | Legitimately write STATE-zone reports/vision/lore, so `Write` is retained; app-code prevention is governed by **zones**, and the implementation-only git mutations are removed |

**`REVIEW_WRITE_EXCEPTIONS`** (in `validate-skill-capabilities.sh`):
`red-teaming`, `bridgebuilder-review`, `spiraling`, `autonomous-agent`,
`run-bridge`, `run-mode`, `reviewing-code`, `auditing-security`. These `role: review` skills keep `Write` by design —
the adversarial/report authors write STATE-zone artifacts, and the autonomous
orchestrators dispatch implementation through the harness (which runs inside
`/implement`, where writes are sanctioned). The validator emits a WARN for any *other* `role: review`
skill that declares `write_files: true` without disallowing `Write` — surfacing
a new C-PROC-001 gap at lint time. `disallowed-tools` is tool-granular, not
path-granular; it cannot express "no `src/` writes but yes `grimoires/` writes",
which is why report-authoring skills rely on zones for path-level control.

## Scope

Applies to every `.claude/skills/**/SKILL.md`. The lint runs as part of the normal validation suite (`bats tests/unit/skill-capabilities.bats`).

## Origin

- Defect: [#553](https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa/issues/553) — `/architect` and `/sprint-plan` produced correct output but refused to write their target files. Three independent reproductions across two repos.
- Tracker: [#557](https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa/issues/557) — Tier 1 cycle-083 framework boundary fixes.
- Sprint: `sprint-bug-102` — test-first patch landing the invariant lint + the three frontmatter fixes.

## Related rules

- [zone-system.md](zone-system.md) — `.claude/` is framework-managed; SKILL.md edits require cycle-level authorization.
- [shell-conventions.md](shell-conventions.md) — file-creation safety when authoring SKILL.md via heredoc.
======
# Git Stash Safety

`git stash push / pop` wraps are risky inside Loa skill execution: pre-commit hooks run their own internal `git stash --keep-index`, an overlapping outer stash shifts the indexes, and `pop` can land on the wrong entry. Combined with output-swallowing (`| tail -N`, `|| true`, `2>/dev/null`) this produces silent data loss that looks like success.

**Mechanically enforced since cycle-122**: `block-destructive-bash.sh` pattern `FR-1.2b` BLOCKS `git stash push/pop/apply` combined with `| tail`/`| head`, `|| true`, or `2>/dev/null` in the same statement — the block message is the repair prompt. This file keeps only the interface and the judgment rules a fence cannot express.

## The safe interface

```bash
source .claude/scripts/stash-safety.sh
stash_with_guard "pre-check" -- run_linter src/   # count-delta enforced, full output surfaced, exit propagated
```

Or sidestep stashing entirely with a worktree (no index-shift window):

```bash
worktree_path="$(mktemp -d)/loa-check"
git worktree add "$worktree_path" HEAD
(cd "$worktree_path" && run_linter src/)
git worktree remove "$worktree_path"
```

## Judgment rules the fence cannot express

- MUST NOT combine `git stash -k` with pre-commit-wrapped operations (the internal `--keep-index` collision is invisible to a command-string fence) — use a worktree.
- SHOULD reach for `git fsck --unreachable | grep commit` BEFORE any `git gc` when recovery is needed — orphaned stashes survive in the object DB only until the next prune.

## Origin

- Defect: [#555](https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa/issues/555) — 4 Edit-tool NOTES.md updates lost to the hazard pattern; recovered only because `git gc --prune=now` hadn't run. Tracker: [#557](https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa/issues/557).
- The hazard shape recurred live during cycle-122 itself (a `git stash pop >/dev/null 2>&1` during a baseline check — caught, verified lossless, and turned into the FR-1.2b fence the same day).

## Related rules

- [shell-conventions.md](shell-conventions.md) — heredoc safety, strict-mode patterns.
- [zone-system.md](zone-system.md) — `.claude/` framework boundary (Bash writes now fenced by FR-SZ2).

1	# .claude/data/floor.yaml — the one tracked floor source (cycle-129 SDD D-9.2, DEC-0166).
     2	#
     3	# The floor is the set of guards, config keys and files no profile, knob or
     4	# cycle task may weaken. Readers:
     5	#   - .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh and tests/unit/guard-origins.bats: the
     6	#     `floor: true` rows of .claude/data/guard-origins.yaml equal floor_guards.
     7	#   - tests/unit/floor-snapshot.bats: every floor_files entry (and the corpus
     8	#     rows named under floor_corpus) is byte-identical to origin/main.
     9	#   - tests/unit/profile-floor.bats (Sprint 2): profiles.yaml names no floor_keys.
    10	# Both bats suites pin this file's sha256; an edit fails until the pin is
    11	# deliberately updated in the same change (see the FLOOR_SHA256 constant).
    12	schema_version: 1
    13	
    14	floor_guards:
    15	  - fence:FR-1.2b
    16	  - fence:FR-SZ
    17	  - fence:FR-SZ-COPY

    49	  - .claude/hooks/settings.deny.json

    51

    53	# origin/main. A trailing `*` is a prefix match.
    54	floor_corpus:
    55	  file: tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl
    56	  rules:
    57	    - FR-1.2b
    58	    - "FR-SZ*"
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
     3	# =============================================================================
     4	# tests/unit/floor-snapshot.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 (PRD AC-1.5, SDD §1.6, D-9.2)
     5	# The floor does not move: every floor_files entry of .claude/data/floor.yaml
     6	# and the fence-corpus rows named under floor_corpus are byte-identical to
     7	# origin/main; the register disables nothing, so the .claude/settings.json hook
     8	# registrations and the fence's pattern-id call-site list are identical too.
     9	# Skipped, with a message, when origin/main is not reachable (a shallow CI
    10	# checkout); the floor.yaml sha256 pin in guard-origins.bats still runs there.
    11	# =============================================================================
    12	
    13	setup() {
    14	  export LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1
    15	  ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd -P)"
    16	  FLOOR="$ROOT/.claude/data/floor.yaml"
    17	  if ! git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --verify -q 'origin/main^{commit}' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    18	    skip "origin/main is not reachable from this checkout (shallow clone?): the floor snapshot needs it — run 'git fetch origin main'"
    19	  fi
    20	  BASE="$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse 'origin/main^{commit}')"
    21	}
    22	
    23	base_show() { git -C "$ROOT" show "$BASE:$1"; }
    24	
    25	@test "FS-1 every floor_files entry is byte-identical to origin/main" {
    26	  n=0
    27	  while IFS= read -r f; do
    28	    [ -n "$f" ] || continue
    29	    n=$((n + 1))
    30	    git -C "$ROOT" cat-file -e "$BASE:$f" || { echo "$f is not on origin/main" >&2; false; }
    31	    base_show "$f" | cmp -s - "$ROOT/$f" || { echo "floor file $f differs from origin/main" >&2; false; }
    32	  done < <(yq -r '.floor_files[]' "$FLOOR")
    33	  [ "$n" -ge 4 ]
    34	}
    35	
    36	@test "FS-2 the fence-corpus rows named in floor_corpus (FR-1.2b, FR-SZ*) are identical to origin/main" {
    37	  corpus="$(yq -r '.floor_corpus.file' "$FLOOR")"
    38	  rules="$(yq -o=json -I0 '.floor_corpus.rules' "$FLOOR")"
    39	  sel='def m($r): $r | any(.[]; . as $p | if ($p | endswith("*")) then ($in.rule // "" | startswith($p | rtrimstr("*"))) else ($in.rule // "") == $p end);
    40	       . as $in | select(m($rules))'
    41	  diff <(base_show "$corpus" | jq -c --argjson rules "$rules" "$sel") <(jq -c --argjson rules "$rules" "$sel" "$ROOT/$corpus")
    42	}
    43	
    44	@test "FS-3 the register disables nothing: settings.json hook registrations are identical to origin/main" {
    45	  diff <(base_show .claude/settings.json | jq -c '.hooks') <(jq -c '.hooks' "$ROOT/.claude/settings.json")
    46	}
    47	
    48	@test "FS-4 the fence's pattern-id call-site list (in order) is identical to origin/main" {
    49	  ids() { grep -oE 'emit_block "[A-Za-z0-9._-]+"|pattern_id(: |=)"[A-Za-z0-9._-]+"'; }
    50	  diff <(base_show .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh | ids) <(ids < "$ROOT/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh")
    51	}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
     3	# =============================================================================
     4	# tests/unit/guard-origins.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 (PRD FR-1 AC-1.1, SDD D-1.6)
     5	# The origin map .claude/data/guard-origins.yaml covers every guard the
     6	# repository enumerates: every hook script registered in .claude/settings.json,
     7	# every fence pattern id in block-destructive-bash.sh, every validator rule
     8	# marker in validate-artifact.sh, the fixed gate list and the floor policies.
     9	# The enumeration here is independent of guard-yield.sh (its own jq/grep), so a
    10	# bug in the script cannot hide a gap. Fixture copies prove the failure modes.
    11	# =============================================================================
    12	
    13	# The sha256 of .claude/data/floor.yaml. An edit to the floor fails this suite
    14	# until the pin is updated deliberately, in the same change, with a reviewer:
    15	#   bash -c 'source .claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh; sha256_portable .claude/data/floor.yaml'
    16	FLOOR_SHA256="bd1f22dce9b6f18a0fda36d5a65dacd8103075c66c8c649b21de04fffcc92587"
    17	
    18	setup() {
    19	  export LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1
    20	  ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd -P)"
    21	  GY="$ROOT/.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh"
    22	  MAP="$ROOT/.claude/data/guard-origins.yaml"
    23	  FLOOR="$ROOT/.claude/data/floor.yaml"
    24	  SETTINGS="$ROOT/.claude/settings.json"
    25	  FENCE="$ROOT/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"
    26	  VALIDATOR="$ROOT/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh"
    27	  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gorig.XXXXXX")"
    28	  # Fixture outputs never touch the tracked register or the live .run.
    29	  OUTARGS=(--out "$T/guards.md" --yield-dir "$T/run" --audit-log "$T/no-audit.jsonl")
    30	}
    31	teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }
    32	
    33	# ids of every registered hook script, derived independently of guard-yield.sh
    34	enumerated_hook_ids() {
    35	  jq -r '.hooks | to_entries[] | .value[] | .hooks[].command' "$SETTINGS" \
    36	    | grep -oE '\.claude/[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+\.sh' | sed -e 's#^\.claude/##' \
    37	    | sed -e 's#^hooks/#hook:#' -e 's#^scripts/#hook:scripts/#' | sort -u
    38	}
    39	enumerated_fence_ids() {
    40	  grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*#' "$FENCE" | grep -oE 'emit_block "[A-Za-z0-9._-]+"|pattern_id(: |=)"[A-Za-z0-9._-]+"' \
    41	    | sed -E 's/.*"([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)"$/fence:\1/' | sort -u
    42	}
    43	enumerated_validator_ids() {
    44	  grep -oE '^[[:space:]]*# @guard validator:[A-Za-z0-9._-]+' "$VALIDATOR" | sed -E 's/.*validator:/validator:/' | sort -u
    45	}
    46	map_ids() { yq -r ".guards[] | select(.kind == \"$1\") | .id" "$MAP" | sort -u; }
    47	
    48	@test "GO-1 the origin map and floor.yaml parse with yq v4 and carry schema_version 1" {
    49	  run yq --version
    50	  [[ "$output" == *mikefarah*"version v4."* ]]
    51	  [ "$(yq '.schema_version' "$MAP")" = "1" ]
    52	  [ "$(yq '.schema_version' "$FLOOR")" = "1" ]
    53	  [ "$(yq '.guards | length' "$MAP")" -gt 0 ]
    54	}
    55	
    56	@test "GO-2 floor.yaml sha256 is pinned (update FLOOR_SHA256 deliberately when the floor changes)" {
    57	  source "$ROOT/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"
    58	  actual="$(sha256_portable "$FLOOR" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
    59	  [ "$actual" = "$FLOOR_SHA256" ] || { echo "floor.yaml sha256 $actual != pinned $FLOOR_SHA256" >&2; false; }
    60	}
    61	
    62	@test "GO-3 every registered hook script has a row with a non-empty origin, and every hook row is registered" {
    63	  hooks="$(enumerated_hook_ids)"
    64	  [ "$(wc -l <<<"$hooks")" -ge 29 ]
    65	  while IFS= read -r id; do
    66	    ref="$(yq -r ".guards[] | select(.id == \"$id\") | .origin.ref // \"\"" "$MAP")"
    67	    [ -n "$ref" ] || { echo "hook $id has no row with an origin" >&2; false; }
    68	  done <<<"$hooks"
    69	  diff <(echo "$hooks") <(map_ids hook)
    70	}
    71	
    72	@test "GO-4 every fence pattern id (emit_block sites and pattern_id constants) has a row, and every fence row is a pattern id" {
    73	  fences="$(enumerated_fence_ids)"
    74	  [ "$(wc -l <<<"$fences")" -ge 32 ]
    75	  grep -qx 'fence:FR-1.2b' <<<"$fences"
    76	  diff <(echo "$fences") <(map_ids fence)
    77	  while IFS= read -r id; do
    78	    [ -n "$(yq -r ".guards[] | select(.id == \"$id\") | .origin.ref // \"\"" "$MAP")" ]
    79	  done <<<"$fences"
    80	}
    81	
    82	@test "GO-5 every validator rule marker has a row, and every validator row has a marker" {
    83	  v="$(enumerated_validator_ids)"
    84	  [ "$(wc -l <<<"$v")" -ge 13 ]
    85	  diff <(echo "$v") <(map_ids validator)
    86	}
    87	
    88	@test "GO-6 the fixed gate list and the floor policies are present and every gate or policy script exists" {
    89	  for g in verdict-derive adversarial-review-gate implement-gate success-criteria dissent-budget seams kinds prompt-budget guard-origins; do
    90	    [ "$(yq -r ".guards[] | select(.id == \"gate:$g\") | .id" "$MAP")" = "gate:$g" ]
    91	  done
    92	  for p in permission-deny-list verdict-one-way-rule operator-only-commands; do
    93	    [ "$(yq -r ".guards[] | select(.id == \"policy:$p\") | .id" "$MAP")" = "policy:$p" ]
    94	  done
    95	  while IFS= read -r s; do
    96	    [ -f "$ROOT/$s" ] || { echo "gate/policy script $s missing" >&2; false; }
    97	  done < <(yq -r '.guards[] | select(.kind == "gate" or .kind == "policy") | .script' "$MAP")
    98	}
    99	
   100	@test "GO-7 the floor: true rows are exactly floor.yaml floor_guards" {
   101	  diff <(yq -r '.floor_guards[]' "$FLOOR" | sort) <(yq -r '.guards[] | select(.floor == true) | .id' "$MAP" | sort)
   102	}
   103

local sanitized_cmd
    sanitized_cmd=$(printf '%s' "$command" | "$redactor" 2>/dev/null) || sanitized_cmd="[REDACTOR-FAILED]"

    # SDD §6.1 v1.1 SKP-008 closure: also redact the matched substring.
    local sanitized_match
    sanitized_match=$(printf '%s' "$matched" | "$redactor" 2>/dev/null) || sanitized_match="[REDACTOR-FAILED]"

    # Truncate AFTER redaction (so partial AKIA prefixes can't slip through).
    if [[ ${#sanitized_cmd} -gt 2048 ]]; then
      sanitized_cmd="${sanitized_cmd:0:2048}[...TRUNCATED]"
    fi
    if [[ ${#sanitized_match} -gt 256 ]]; then
      sanitized_match="${sanitized_match:0:256}[...TRUNCATED]"
    fi

    mkdir -p "${LOA_REPO_ROOT:-.}/.run" 2>/dev/null || true

    # perf pass-2: UTC timestamp via bash strftime (was `date -u` spawn);
    # cwd via $PWD (bash keeps it identical to the pwd builtin's output).
    local _ts
    TZ=UTC0 printf -v _ts '%(%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)T' -1

    jq -cn \
      --arg ts "$_ts" \
      --arg cmd "$sanitized_cmd" \
      --arg cwd "$PWD" \
      --arg model "${LOA_CURRENT_MODEL:-}" \
      --arg provider "${LOA_CURRENT_PROVIDER:-}" \
      --arg trace_id "${LOA_TRACE_ID:-}" \
      --arg team_id "${LOA_TEAM_ID:-}" \
      --arg team_member "${LOA_TEAM_MEMBER:-}" \
      --arg pattern_id "$pattern_id" \
      --arg matched "$sanitized_match" \
      --arg replay "${LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY:-}" \
      '{ts: $ts, tool: "Bash", command: $cmd, exit_code: 2, cwd: $cwd, model: $model, provider: $provider, trace_id: $trace_id, team_id: $team_id, team_member: $team_member, hook: "block-destructive-bash", action: "block", pattern_id: $pattern_id, matched: $matched} + (if $replay == "1" then {replay: true} else {} end)' \
      >> "${LOA_REPO_ROOT:-.}/.run/audit.jsonl" 2>/dev/null || true
  } 2>/dev/null || true

  exit 2
}

# Backward-compat helper: existing call sites used check_and_block. Keep it
# as a thin wrapper that funnels through emit_block with pattern_id="LEGACY".
# All new direct callers should use emit_block with a real pattern_id.
check_and_block() {
  local pattern="$1"
  emit_block "FR-1.2" "$matched" "git stash {drop,clear} permanently destroys stashed work. Run 'git stash list' first; consider 'git stash show' / 'git stash apply' before dropping."
fi

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# P6b — stash output-swallowing (FR-1.2b, cycle-122, issue #555 shapes)
# git stash push/pop/apply with its output truncated (| tail / | head),
# error stream suppressed (2>/dev/null), or exit masked (|| true) hides
# CONFLICT lines and wrong-slot pops — the exact silent-data-loss chain from
# #555 (4 NOTES.md edits lost; recovered only because gc hadn't pruned).
# `[^;&|]*` keeps the swallow-operator in the SAME statement segment as the
# stash call. `\|\|` (masking) vs `\|` (pipe) are distinguished by the
# alternation order + explicit true operand.
# pass-8 pre-filter: `stash` plus one of the swallow literals.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# @guard fence:FR-1.2b
if [[ "$command" == *"stash"* && ( "$command" == *"tail"* || "$command" == *"head"* || "$command" == *"/dev/null"* || "$command" == *"true"* ) ]] \
   && _match '(^|/|;|&&|\||[[:space:]]|\(|'"'"'|")[[:space:]]*(sudo[[:space:]]+)?git[[:space:]]+stash[[:space:]]+(push|pop|apply)[^;&|]*(\|[[:space:]]*(tail|head)([[:space:]]|$)|\|\|[[:space:]]*true([[:space:]]*([;&|#]|$))|(&|[0-9]*)>>?[[:space:]]*/dev/null)'; then
  matched=$(echo "$command" | grep -oE 'git[[:space:]]+stash[[:space:]]+(push|pop|apply)[^;&|]*.{0,20}' | head -1)
  emit_block "FR-1.2b" "$matched" "Output-swallowing (pipe-truncate, exit-mask, or ANY /dev/null redirect) around git stash push/pop/apply hides CONFLICT lines and wrong-slot pops (silent data loss, issue #555). Use stash_with_guard from .claude/scripts/stash-safety.sh, or run the stash bare and read its FULL output. Rules: .claude/rules/stash-safety.md"
fi

    if [[ ! -f "$suite_file" ]]; then

      exit 3
    fi

    # Read include patterns from suite
    local include_count
    include_count="$(yq -r '.tasks.include | length // 0' "$suite_file")"

    for i in $(seq 0 $((include_count - 1))); do
      local pattern
      pattern="$(yq -r ".tasks.include[$i]" "$suite_file")"

      # Resolve glob pattern relative to evals/
      # Use bash globbing with globstar for ** patterns
      local had_globstar=false
      shopt -q globstar 2>/dev/null && had_globstar=true
      shopt -s globstar 2>/dev/null || true

      local glob_expanded=false
      for task_file in $EVALS_DIR/$pattern; do
        if [[ -f "$task_file" ]]; then
          TASK_FILES+=("$task_file")
          glob_expanded=true
        fi
      done

      # Restore globstar
      if [[ "$had_globstar" == "false" ]]; then
        shopt -u globstar 2>/dev/null || true
      fi

      # Fallback: if glob didn't match, try find in the directory
      if [[ "$glob_expanded" == "false" ]]; then
        # Extract directory portion from pattern
        local pattern_dir="${pattern%/*}"
        if [[ -d "$EVALS_DIR/$pattern_dir" ]]; then
          while IFS= read -r -d '' task_file; do
            TASK_FILES+=("$task_file")
          done < <(find "$EVALS_DIR/$pattern_dir" \( -name '*.yaml' -o -name '*.yml' \) -type f -print0 2>/dev/null)
        fi
      fi
    done

    # Apply exclude patterns
    local exclude_count
    exclude_count="$(yq -r '.tasks.exclude | length // 0' "$suite_file" 2>/dev/null || echo "0")"
    if [[ "$exclude_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
      local filtered_tasks=()
      for task_file in "${TASK_FILES[@]}"; do
        local excluded=false
        for j in $(seq 0 $((exclude_count - 1))); do
          local exclude_pattern
          exclude_pattern="$(yq -r ".tasks.exclude[$j]" "$suite_file")"
          if [[ "$(basename "$task_file")" == $exclude_pattern ]]; then
            excluded=true
            break
          fi
        done
        [[ "$excluded" == "false" ]] && filtered_tasks+=("$task_file")
      done
      TASK_FILES=("${filtered_tasks[@]}")
    fi

    # Read suite defaults
    SUITE_TRIALS="$(yq -r '.defaults.trials // 1' "$suite_file")"
    SUITE_TIMEOUT_TRIAL="$(yq -r '.defaults.timeout.per_trial // 120' "$suite_file")"

    log "[LOAD] Suite '$SUITE': ${#TASK_FILES[@]} tasks, ${SUITE_TRIALS} trial(s)"
    return
  fi

  # Default: run all tasks
  while IFS= read -r -d '' task_file; do
    TASK_FILES+=("$task_file")
  done < <(find "$TASKS_DIR" -name '*.yaml' -o -name '*.yml' | sort | tr '\n' '\0')

# @guard validator:sprint.sections
SPRINT_REQUIRED_SECTIONS=(
    "Sprint Goal"
    "Deliverables"
    "Acceptance Criteria"
    "Technical Tasks"
    "Dependencies"
    "Risks & Mitigation"
    "Success Metrics"
)
SPRINT_WARN_SECTIONS=(
    "Security Considerations"
)

validate_sprint() {
    local sprint_headings
    sprint_headings=$(grep -nE '^## Sprint [0-9]' -- "$FILE" || true)

    if [[ -z "$sprint_headings" ]]; then
        violations+=("no '## Sprint N' blocks found — sprint.md must contain at least one sprint block")
        return
    fi

    local last_sprint_heading="" last_sprint_lineno=0
    while IFS=: read -r lineno heading; do
        [[ -z "$lineno" ]] && continue
        last_sprint_heading="$heading"
        last_sprint_lineno="$lineno"
        local block
        block=$(awk -v start="$lineno" '
            NR > start && /^## Sprint [0-9]/ { exit }
            NR > start { print }
        ' < "$FILE")
        local sec
        for sec in "${SPRINT_REQUIRED_SECTIONS[@]}"; do
            if ! grep -qE "^### ($sec)\$" <<< "$block"; then
                violations+=("sprint block '${heading# }' (line $lineno) is missing required section '### $sec' — see planning-sprints/resources/templates/sprint-template.md")
            fi
        done
        for sec in "${SPRINT_WARN_SECTIONS[@]}"; do
            if ! grep -qE "^### ($sec)\$" <<< "$block"; then
                warnings+=("sprint block '${heading# }' (line $lineno) has no '### $sec' section — recommended for security-relevant sprints")
            fi
        done
    done <<< "$sprint_headings"

    # @guard validator:sprint.goal-ids
    # Goal ID coverage: every G-N referenced in the plan body must appear in
    # a goal-mapping table under any '## Appendix' section.
    local appendix_body
    appendix_body=$(awk '
        /^## Appendix/ { found=1; next }
        found && /^## / { found=0 }
        found { print }
    ' < "$FILE")

    local body_goal_ids
    body_goal_ids=$(grep -oE 'G-[0-9]+' -- "$FILE" | sort -u || true)
    if [[ -n "$body_goal_ids" ]]; then
        while IFS= read -r gid; do
            [[ -z "$gid" ]] && continue
            if ! grep -qwF "$gid" <<< "$appendix_body"; then
                violations+=("goal ID $gid appears in the plan but not in any '## Appendix' goal table — add a row for $gid")
            fi
        done <<< "$body_goal_ids"
    fi

    validate_sprint_deferred
    validate_sprint_seams
    validate_sprint_kinds
    validate_sprint_beads

    # Final sprint E2E/validation task (WARN only).
    local last_block
    last_block=$(awk -v start="$last_sprint_lineno" 'NR > start { print }' < "$FILE")
    if ! grep -qiE 'E2E|end-to-end' <<< "$last_block"; then
        warnings+=("final sprint block '${last_sprint_heading# }' has no E2E/end-to-end validation task")
    fi
}

+++ head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh	2026-10-21 04:04:22.820694000 +0000

 #   EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN     CLI executable                     (default: claude)
 #   EVAL_MAX_TURNS      --max-turns                        (default 40)
 #
-# Tested by evals/tests/execute-agent.bats.
+# Control arms (cycle-129 FR-2, SDD D-2.1):
+#   LOA_EVAL_ARM          arm id (default baseline). Setting it at all is "arm
+#                         mode": the prompt tree's .loa.config.yaml is also
+#                         materialised so every arm sees the same config.
+#   LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES  JSON object {toggle: false, …}; when unset the arm is
+#                         resolved from LOA_EVAL_SUITE_FILE, else from
+#                         evals/suites/<task dir name>.yaml (`ab.arms[]`)
+#   LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT  recorded as source_commit (default: the prompt
+#                         tree's HEAD)
+#   Toggles are applied to the SANDBOX COPY only, after every materialisation
+#   step and immediately before the executor starts; each is verified absent
+#   afterwards and a toggle that cannot take effect is exit 2 (an arm never
+#   silently runs as its baseline):
+#     companion_voice: false         flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice=false
+#                                    in <ws>/.loa.config.yaml (yq)
+#     karpathy_block: false          '## Karpathy Principles' section out of
+#                                    <ws>/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md; Karpathy rows
+#                                    out of <ws>/.claude/data/constraints.json if present
+#     rule_files: false              stash-safety.md, skill-invariants.md out of <ws>/.claude/rules/
+#     audit_delta_instruction: false the paragraph containing "look for what the
+#                                    review did not", else "Confirm the review's demotions
+#                                    independently", out of the sandbox auditing-security/SKILL.md
+#   The appended skill prompt (.eval/skill-prompt.md) is derived from the
+#   toggled sandbox SKILL.md. executor.json records arm, arm_toggles,
+#   arm_evidence and source_commit.
+#
+# Tested by evals/tests/execute-agent.bats and evals/tests/arm-toggles.bats.
 # =============================================================================
 set -euo pipefail
 
@@ -123,9 +149,140 @@
 fi
 printf '@.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md\n' > "$WORKSPACE/CLAUDE.md"
 
-# Skill body without the YAML frontmatter → the appended system prompt.
+# --- 2b. control arm (cycle-129 FR-2) -----------------------------------------
+ARM_MODE=false
+[[ -n "${LOA_EVAL_ARM+x}" ]] && ARM_MODE=true
+ARM="${LOA_EVAL_ARM:-baseline}"
+[[ "$ARM" =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$ ]] || { echo "ERROR: invalid LOA_EVAL_ARM '$ARM'" >&2; exit 2; }
+if [[ "$ARM_MODE" == "true" && -f "$PROMPT_TREE/.loa.config.yaml" ]]; then
+  cp "$PROMPT_TREE/.loa.config.yaml" "$WORKSPACE/.loa.config.yaml"
+fi
+
+# The arm's toggles: explicit JSON, else the suite's ab.arms[] entry.
+resolve_toggles() {
+  if [[ -n "${LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES:-}" ]]; then
+    jq -ce 'if type == "object" then . else error("not an object") end' <<<"$LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES" 2>/dev/null \
+      || { echo "ERROR: LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES is not a JSON object" >&2; return 2; }
+    return 0
+  fi
+  local suite_file="${LOA_EVAL_SUITE_FILE:-}"
+  if [[ -z "$suite_file" ]]; then
+    local tdir; tdir="$(basename "$(dirname "$TASK_YAML")")"
+    [[ -f "$REPO_ROOT/evals/suites/$tdir.yaml" ]] && suite_file="$REPO_ROOT/evals/suites/$tdir.yaml"
+  fi
+  local t="" found=0
+  if [[ -n "$suite_file" && -f "$suite_file" ]]; then
+    found="$(ARM="$ARM" yq '[.ab.arms[]? | select(.id == strenv(ARM))] | length' "$suite_file" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
+    [[ "$found" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || found=0
+    if [[ "$found" -gt 0 ]]; then
+      t="$(ARM="$ARM" yq -o=json -I=0 '[.ab.arms[] | select(.id == strenv(ARM))][0].toggles // {}' "$suite_file" 2>/dev/null)"
+    fi
+  fi
+  if [[ "$found" -eq 0 || -z "$t" || "$t" == "null" ]]; then
+    [[ "$ARM" == "baseline" ]] && { printf '{}'; return 0; }
+    echo "ERROR: arm '$ARM' is not declared in ${suite_file:-any suite} (ab.arms[])" >&2
+    return 2
+  fi
+  printf '%s' "$t"
+}
+ARM_TOGGLES="$(resolve_toggles)" || exit 2
+
+# Remove the markdown section that starts at the exact heading line $2 (up to
+# the next level-2 heading) from file $1. Prints the number of lines removed.
+_drop_md_section() {
+  local f="$1" heading="$2" tmp
+  tmp="$(mktemp "$eval_dir/.arm.XXXXXX")"
+  awk -v h="$heading" '
+    $0 == h { skip = 1; n++; next }
+    skip && /^## / { skip = 0 }
+    skip { n++; next }
+    { print }
+    END { print n + 0 > "/dev/stderr" }' "$f" > "$tmp" 2> "$tmp.n"
+  mv "$tmp" "$f"
+  cat "$tmp.n"; rm -f "$tmp.n"
+}
+
+# Remove the first blank-line-delimited paragraph of $1 that contains one of
+# the needles (tried in order, case-insensitive). Writes the removed text to
+# $2; exit 1 when no needle matches.
+_drop_paragraph() {
+  python3 -I - "$1" "$2" "look for what the review did not" "Confirm the review's demotions independently" <<'PY'
+import re, sys
+path, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
+text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
+paras = re.split(r"(\n[ \t]*\n)", text)
+for needle in sys.argv[3:]:
+    for i in range(0, len(paras), 2):
+        if needle.lower() in paras[i].lower():
+            removed = paras[i]
+            # drop the paragraph and the separator that follows it
+            del paras[i:i + 2]
+            open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write("".join(paras))
+            open(out, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(removed + "\n")
+            sys.exit(0)
+sys.exit(1)
+PY
+}
+
+ARM_EVIDENCE='{}'
+_evidence() { ARM_EVIDENCE="$(jq -c --arg k "$1" --arg v "$2" '. + {($k): $v}' <<<"$ARM_EVIDENCE")"; }
+
+apply_toggles() {
+  local key val
+  while IFS=$'\t' read -r key val; do
+    [[ -n "$key" ]] || continue
+    if [[ "$val" != "false" ]]; then
+      echo "ERROR: arm '$ARM' toggle $key=$val (only false is defined)" >&2; return 2
+    fi
+    case "$key" in
+      companion_voice)
+        local cfg="$WORKSPACE/.loa.config.yaml"
+        [[ -f "$cfg" ]] || : > "$cfg"
+        yq -i '.flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice = false | .flatline_protocol.security_audit.companion_voice = false' "$cfg" \
+          || { echo "ERROR: companion_voice toggle: yq failed on the sandbox config" >&2; return 2; }
+        [[ "$(yq -r '.flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice' "$cfg")" == "false" ]] \
+          || { echo "ERROR: companion_voice toggle did not take effect" >&2; return 2; }
+        _evidence companion_voice "flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice=false"
+        ;;
+      karpathy_block)
+        local k="$WORKSPACE/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" n
+        [[ -f "$k" ]] || { echo "ERROR: karpathy_block toggle: no sandbox CLAUDE.loa.md" >&2; return 2; }
+        n="$(_drop_md_section "$k" '## Karpathy Principles')"
+        if [[ "${n:-0}" -eq 0 ]] || grep -q '^## Karpathy Principles' "$k"; then
+          echo "ERROR: karpathy_block toggle: no '## Karpathy Principles' section removed" >&2; return 2
+        fi
+        local cj="$WORKSPACE/.claude/data/constraints.json"
+        if [[ -f "$cj" ]]; then
+          jq '(.constraints // []) |= map(select((tostring | test("karpathy"; "i")) | not))' "$cj" > "$cj.tmp" && mv "$cj.tmp" "$cj"

content.content:
1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""arms-report.py — the cycle-129 FR-2 control-arm report (SDD D-2.3).
     3	
     4	Invoked by `report.sh --arms`. Reads <results-root>/<suite>/STATUS.json (the
     5	suite aggregate run-arms.sh writes), every batch's MANIFEST.json and
     6	<arm>/results.jsonl, and the suite's pre-registered `ab.threshold` and
     7	`ab.arms`, and writes one markdown report.
     8	
     9	Per arm: recall (mean over defect fixtures of the per-fixture trial mean;
    10	the min, max and spread of the per-trial means), refuted share (cited
    11	findings matching neither a feedback label nor a fix region, over cited
    12	findings, pooled over completed trials), tokens per call, the percentile
    13	bootstrap interval of the recall drop (baseline - arm) resampling fixtures,
    14	the verdict and the missed labels.
    15	
    16	Verdict (pre-registered; never computed for baseline):
    17	  inconclusive  --partial; the run is not complete; a planned fixture lacks
    18	                trials_required completed trials in the arm or the baseline;
    19	                model or source skew; no defect fixture; or only a recall
    20	                rule is violated while the mean drop does not exceed the
    21	                baseline's own trial-to-trial spread (a change too small to name)
    22	  recall loss   the refuted-share rule is violated, or a recall rule is
    23	                violated and the mean drop exceeds the baseline spread
    24	  no recall loss  every rule holds:
    25	                  upper bound of the drop interval <= mean_recall_max_drop
    26	                  arm min trial mean >= baseline min trial mean - min_trial_recall_max_drop
    27	                  arm refuted share <= baseline refuted share + refuted_share_max_rise
    28	An `informational: true` arm's verdict reports a yield only.
    29	
    30	Exit: 0 written, 1 refused (a suite is not complete and --partial was not
    31	given), 2 error. Stdlib only.
    32	"""
    33	import argparse
    34	import datetime
    35	import json
    36	import os
    37	import random
    38	import sys
    39	from collections import Counter, defaultdict
    40	
    41	
    42	def load_yaml_subset(path):
    43	    """The suites are YAML (no stdlib parser); the harness already depends on yq v4."""
    44	    import subprocess
    45	    out = subprocess.run(["yq", "-o=json", ".", path], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    46	    return json.loads(out)
    47	
    48	
    49	def read_jsonl(path):
    50	    rows = []
    51	    if not os.path.isfile(path):
    52	        return rows
    53	    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    54	        for line in fh:
    55	            line = line.strip()
    56	            if line:
    57	                try:
    58	                    rows.append(json.loads(line))
    59	                except ValueError:
    60	                    continue
    61	    return rows
    62	
    63	
    64	def mean(xs):
    65	    xs = [x for x in xs if x is not None]
    66	    return sum(xs) / len(xs) if xs else None
    67	
    68	
    69	def fmt(x, nd=3):
    70	    return "n/a" if x is None else f"{x:.{nd}f}"
    71	
    72	
    73	def recall_details(row):
    74	    for g in row.get("graders") or []:
    75	        if g.get("name") == "recall-vs-defects.sh" and isinstance(g.get("details"), dict):
    76	            return g["details"]
    77	    return None
    78	
    79	
    80	def tokens(row):
    81	    u = (row.get("executor") or {}).get("usage") or {}
    82	    if not u:
    83	        return None
    84	    return sum(int(u.get(k, 0) or 0) for k in
    85	               ("input_tokens", "cache_creation_input_tokens", "cache_read_input_tokens", "output_tokens"))
    86	
    87	
    88	def percentile(sorted_xs, q):
    89	    if not sorted_xs:
    90	        return None
    91	    k = max(0, min(len(sorted_xs) - 1, int(round(q * (len(sorted_xs) - 1)))))
    92	    return sorted_xs[k]
    93	
    94	
    95	def bootstrap(deltas, iterations, level, seed):
    96	    """Percentile bootstrap of the mean of per-fixture deltas (resample fixtures)."""
    97	    if not deltas:
    98	        return None, None
    99	    rng = random.Random(seed)
   100	    n = len(deltas)
   101	    means = sorted(sum(deltas[rng.randrange(n)] for _ in range(n)) / n for _ in range(iterations))
   102	    a = (1.0 - level) / 2.0
   103	    return percentile(means, a), percentile(means, 1.0 - a)
   104	
   105	
   106	class Arm:
   107	    def __init__(self, arm_id):
   108	        self.id = arm_id
   109	        self.cells = defaultdict(list)   # fixture -> [(trial, recall)], every completed trial kept
   110	        self.planted = {}                # fixture -> planted count
   111	        self.cited = 0
   112	        self.refuted = 0
   113	        self.tokens = []
   114	        self.models = set()
   115	        self.sources = set()
   116	        self.done = 0
   117	        self.errors = 0
   118	        self.fallback_trials = 0         # trials the CLI moved to another model on a safeguard refusal
   119	        self.fallback_kinds = Counter()
   120	        self.missed = Counter()          # (fixture, label) -> trials missed
   121	        self.seen = Counter()            # (fixture, label) -> trials graded
   122	
   123	    def add(self, row):
   124	        if row.get("status") != "completed":
   125	            self.errors += 1
   126	            return
   127	        d = recall_details(row)
   128	        if d is None:
   129	            self.errors += 1
   130	            return
   131	        self.done += 1
   132	        fx = row.get("fixture") or row.get("task_id", "").split("-", 1)[-1]
   133	        self.planted[fx] = int(d.get("planted") or 0)
   134	        if d.get("recall") is not None:
   135	            self.cells[fx].append((int(row.get("trial") or 0), float(d["recall"])))
   136	        if d.get("findings_cited") is not None:
   137	            self.cited += int(d.get("findings_cited") or 0)
   138	            self.refuted += int(d.get("findings_refuted") or 0)
   139	        t = tokens(row)
   140	        if t is not None:
   141	            self.tokens.append(t)
   142	        self.models.add(row.get("model_id") or (row.get("executor") or {}).get("model_id"))
   143	        # every model that produced output in the call (an auxiliary model is skew too)
   144	        for mid, out in ((row.get("executor") or {}).get("models_used") or {}).items():
   145	            if out:
   146	                self.models.add(mid)
   147	        fb = (row.get("executor") or {}).get("refusal_fallbacks") or []
   148	        if fb:
   149	            self.fallback_trials += 1
   150	            for x in fb:
   151	                self.fallback_kinds[f"{x.get('from')}→{x.get('to')} ({x.get('category')})"] += 1
   152	        self.sources.add(row.get("source_commit") or (row.get("executor") or {}).get("source_commit"))

     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# evals/tests/run-arms.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 Task 1.6 (FR-2, SDD D-2.3)
     4	#
     5	# run-arms.sh drives control arms over a frozen fixture batch against a
     6	# detached worktree pinned at --source-commit. The executor is the CLI stub
     7	# (no model call); the source repo is a throwaway repo (LOA_ARMS_SOURCE_REPO)
     8	# so no worktree is ever registered in the real repository; the results and
     9	# the worktree live under the test's temp dir.
    10	# =============================================================================
    11	
    12	setup() {
    13	  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
    14	  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    15	  RA="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/run-arms.sh"
    16	  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ra.XXXXXX")"
    17	  SRC="$T/src"
    18	  mkdir -p "$SRC/.claude/loa" "$SRC/.claude/rules" "$SRC/.claude/skills/reviewing-code"
    19	  printf '%s\n' "# Loa" "" "## Karpathy Principles" "" "k" "" "## Other" > "$SRC/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    20	  echo "# s" > "$SRC/.claude/rules/stash-safety.md"
    21	  echo "# i" > "$SRC/.claude/rules/skill-invariants.md"

    23	  printf '%s\n' "flatline_protocol:" "  code_review:" "    enabled: true" > "$SRC/.loa.config.yaml"

53:**Judgment**: The task kind for work that needs reading and a decision; it ships as prose or a reviewed artifact, and its sprint task line ends with kind: judgment.
60:**Kind counts**: The release-notes line that counts a cycle's sprint tasks by kind (mechanical, judgment and operator), read from the tagged task lines of its sprint plan.
69:**Mechanical**: The task kind for work a script could do reliably; it ships as code with tests, and a review flags a mechanical task delivered as prose the model re-executes.
71:**Operator**: The human who owns the project and its decisions; as a task kind, work that belongs to that human, which a review flags when it was completed unattended without a decision:unblock ticket or a DEC row.
89:**Volume ratio**: The release-notes line that sets a cycle's script lines changed against its prose bytes changed and its model calls; the model-call count is local to the host that ran the cycle.

display_artefacts_line() {
  local g="${LOA_GRIMOIRE_DIR:-$PROJECT_ROOT/grimoires/loa}" guard="${SCRIPT_DIR}/notes-guard.sh"
  local f b line="" warn=""
  for f in prd.md sdd.md sprint.md NOTES.md; do
    [[ -f "$g/$f" ]] || continue
    b=$(stat -c%s "$g/$f" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    line+=" ${f%.md} $(( (b + 1023) / 1024 ))K"
    if [[ -f "$guard" ]] && bash "$guard" check --file "$g/$f" 2>&1 >/dev/null | grep -q 'NOTES-WARN\|NOTES-BLOCK'; then
      warn+=" $f"
    fi
  done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# guard-yield.sh — the guard register and its 30-day host yield (cycle-129 FR-1)
# =============================================================================
# Enumerates every guard Loa ships and joins it with its origin and its yield:
#   hooks       every command registered in .claude/settings.json, parsed against
#               the canonical schema "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"/.claude/<path> [args]
#               (or the same wrapped in hook-guard.sh); one row per unique script
#   fences      the `# @guard fence:<id>` markers in block-destructive-bash.sh,
#               cross-checked both ways against its emit_block call sites and
#               its literal `pattern_id: "<id>"` audit constants
#   validators  the `# @guard validator:<id>` markers in validate-artifact.sh
#   gates       the fixed list in the origin map (each row's `script` must exist)
#   policies    the floor policies in the origin map
# Origins, class, status, knob and floor come from .claude/data/guard-origins.yaml;
# the floor set must equal .claude/data/floor.yaml floor_guards.
#
# Outputs:
#   grimoires/loa/guards.md        tracked, STRUCTURAL ONLY (a pure function of the
#                                  repository; no timestamp, no yield) — --check gates it
#   .run/guard-yield.md, .json     untracked host yield: blocks_30d, likely_fp_30d,
#                                  telemetry_30d, last_real_catch per guard
#   hooks-reference.md table       with --hooks-table, the rows between
#                                  <!-- guard-register:begin --> and <!-- guard-register:end -->
#
# Yield (SDD D-1.3): rows of .run/audit.jsonl and its rotated segments
# .run/audit.jsonl.* with action == "block", plus implement-gate rows (telemetry
# when action is telemetry or ask), with ts inside the window. Replays are
# excluded and counted: replay == true (LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1 at the source), or,
# for rows that predate the flag, a cwd under ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ or containing
# /bats-run-, /bats., /evals/results/ or /sandbox/, or a UTC minute holding
# BURST_ROWS (10) or more block rows (a suite replaying fixtures into the live
# log from inside the repository; no interactive session blocks ten commands in
# one minute). A block is a likely false
# positive (a heuristic) when its command holds a heredoc (`<<`; or, when
# .claude/scripts/lib/heredoc-classifier.sh defines heredoc_nonexec, a heredoc
# that function calls non-executing), when its cwd lies outside the repository
# (this checkout and its main worktree), or when its pattern id is a prose class
# (SP-1, FR-MERGE-2, FR-2-AMBIGUOUS) with no destructive verb at statement start.
# A real catch is a block that is not a likely false positive.
#
# Privacy: no command text, cwd, hostname, user or model name is written to any
# output; ids match ^[A-Za-z0-9._/:-]+$; origin text comes from the tracked map.
#
# Usage:
#   guard-yield.sh [--window-days 30] [--audit-log PATH] [--origins PATH]
#                  [--floor PATH] [--out grimoires/loa/guards.md] [--yield-dir .run]
#                  [--hooks-table] [--check] [--json] [--root DIR]
#                  [--settings PATH] [--fence PATH] [--validator PATH]
#                  [--hooks-ref PATH] [--now YYYY-MM-DD|YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ|EPOCH]
#
# Exit codes:
#   0  written, or in sync (--check)
#   1  drift (--check): guards.md or the hooks table differ from what would be written
#   2  usage error
#   3  unreadable or unparseable input (a missing audit log is a WARN and an empty yield)
#   5  a guard without an origin row, a row that resolves to nothing, an invalid row,
#      a floor mismatch, or a hook command outside the canonical schema
#
# Tested by tests/unit/guard-yield.bats and tests/unit/guard-origins.bats.
15:# Origins, class, status, knob and floor come from .claude/data/guard-origins.yaml;
20:#                                  repository; no timestamp, no yield) — --check gates it
23:#   hooks-reference.md table       with --hooks-table, the rows between

# md-fence.awk: fenced-code tracking for markdown readers written in awk.
#
# md_fence(line) returns 1 when the line opens, closes or sits inside a fenced
# code block and 0 for a line of ordinary text. Call it once per line, in order.
# A fence opens on a line of at least three backticks or tildes (leading
# whitespace allowed); a backtick opener's info string may not contain a
# backtick. It closes only on a line of the same character, at least as long
# as the opener, followed by nothing but whitespace (CommonMark). So a
# four-backtick block may contain three-backtick lines, and a tilde line
# inside a backtick block is plain content.
#
# Shared by tools/check-glossary-terms.sh and validate-artifact.sh
# --type glossary; they prepend this text to their own program, so it must
# stay POSIX awk (mawk, one-true-awk and busybox awk all run it).
function md_fence(line,   t, ch, n, rest) {
    t = line
    sub(/^[[:space:]]+/, "", t)
    ch = substr(t, 1, 1)
    n = 0
    if (ch == "`" || ch == "~") {
        while (substr(t, n + 1, 1) == ch) n++
    }
    rest = substr(t, n + 1)
    if (!_md_fence_len) {
        if (n < 3) return 0
        if (ch == "`" && index(rest, "`")) return 0
        _md_fence_ch = ch; _md_fence_len = n
        return 1
    }
    if (ch == _md_fence_ch && n >= _md_fence_len && rest !~ /[^[:space:]]/) _md_fence_len = 0
    return 1
}

# Gated on the header **Date:** exactly as the Seams rule above: from KINDS_REQUIRED_FROM
# on, every top-level '- [ ]' / '- [x]' line under '### Technical Tasks', and every
# '- [ ] Task ...' line under a '### Task N.E2E' heading, inside a '## Sprint N' block,
# ends with exactly one 'kind: mechanical|judgment|operator' token (whitespace around the
# colon allowed, nothing but whitespace after the value; the ⇐ dependency marker may be
# absent). Older and undated plans WARN once; a live plan without a parseable header date
# fails. Inline code spans are not tokens. A 'judgment' task that names only *.sh, *.py or
# *.ts files, or the verbs script, lint or generate, WARNs (never fails).
# @guard validator:sprint.kinds
KINDS_REQUIRED_FROM="2026-10-14"

validate_sprint_kinds() {
    local fence_src
    if ! fence_src="$(cat "${SCRIPT_DIR}/lib/md-fence.awk" 2>/dev/null)" || [[ -z "$fence_src" ]]; then
        violations+=("cannot read ${SCRIPT_DIR}/lib/md-fence.awk; the sprint kind: check needs it (reinstall the framework scripts)")
        return 0
    fi
    local plan_date
    plan_date="$(LC_ALL=C awk "$fence_src"'
        md_fence($0) { next }
        /^## / { exit }
        /^\*\*Date:?\*\*:?/ { if (match($0, /[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]/)) print substr($0, RSTART, RLENGTH); exit }
    ' "$FILE")"
    local enforce=false canon="" root=""
    if [[ -n "$plan_date" ]]; then
        [[ "$plan_date" < "$KINDS_REQUIRED_FROM" ]] || enforce=true
    else
        canon="$(cd "$(dirname -- "$FILE")" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)/$(basename -- "$FILE")" || canon=""
        root="$(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)" || root=""
        if [[ -n "$root" ]]; then
            case "$canon" in
                "${root}/grimoires/loa/archive/"*) ;;
                "${root}/grimoires/loa/"*)
                    violations+=("a sprint plan carries **Date:** YYYY-MM-DD in its header (before the first '## ' heading); ${FILE} has none that parses, so the kind: rule (from ${KINDS_REQUIRED_FROM}) cannot be judged")
                    return 0 ;;
            esac
        fi
    fi
    local findings
    findings="$(LC_ALL=C awk "$fence_src"'
        function ntok(s,   n) {
            n = 0
            while (match(s, /(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])kind[[:space:]]*:/)) { n++; s = substr(s, RSTART + RLENGTH) }
            return n
        }
        md_fence($0) { next }
        /^## / { insp = ($0 ~ /^## Sprint [0-9]/); sec = 0; next }
        !insp { next }
        /^### / {
            sec = 0
            if ($0 ~ /^### Technical Tasks[[:space:]]*$/) sec = 1
            else if ($0 ~ /^### Task [0-9A-Za-z]+\.E2E([^A-Za-z0-9]|$)/) sec = 2
            next
        }
        !sec || $0 !~ /^- \[[ xX]\] / { next }
        sec == 2 && $0 !~ /^- \[[ xX]\] Task / { next }
        {
            raw = $0; t = raw
            gsub(/`[^`]*`/, "", t)
            n = ntok(t)
            if (n == 0) { printf "M\t%d\t0\n", NR; next }
            if (n > 1) { printf "D\t%d\t%d\n", NR, n; next }
            if (raw !~ /(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])kind[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*(mechanical|judgment|operator)[[:space:]]*$/) {
                if (t ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])kind[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*(mechanical|judgment|operator)([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)/) printf "T\t%d\t0\n", NR
                else printf "U\t%d\t0\n", NR
                next
            }
            if (raw !~ /judgment[[:space:]]*$/) next
            files = 0; code = 0; s = raw
            while (match(s, /[A-Za-z0-9_.\/*-]+\.(sh|py|ts|js|md|yaml|yml|json|tsv|bats|txt|toml)([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)/)) {
                tok = substr(s, RSTART, RLENGTH); s = substr(s, RSTART + RLENGTH)
                files++
                if (tok ~ /\.(sh|py|ts)([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)/) code++
            }
            v = tolower(t)
            if ((files > 0 && files == code) || v ~ /(^|[^a-z0-9_])(script|lint|generate)([^a-z0-9_]|$)/) printf "J\t%d\t0\n", NR
        }
    ' "$FILE")"
    [[ -n "$findings" ]] || return 0
    local code ln extra
    local -a bad=()
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r code ln extra; do
        case "$code" in
            J) warnings+=("$FILE:$ln: a task tagged kind: judgment names only *.sh/*.py/*.ts files or the verbs script, lint, generate; if a script could do it reliably, tag it kind: mechanical") ;;
            M) bad+=("$FILE:$ln: a task line has no kind: token; end it with ' · kind: mechanical|judgment|operator'") ;;
            D) bad+=("$FILE:$ln: a task line carries ${extra} kind: tokens; keep exactly one, at the end of the line") ;;
            T) bad+=("$FILE:$ln: a task line has text after its kind: value; the kind: token ends the line") ;;
            U) bad+=("$FILE:$ln: a task line's kind: value is not one of mechanical, judgment, operator (lower case)") ;;
        esac
    done <<< "$findings"
    [[ ${#bad[@]} -gt 0 ]] || return 0
    if [[ "$enforce" == "true" ]]; then
        local b
        for b in "${bad[@]}"; do
            violations+=("${b} (a plan dated ${plan_date}, on or after ${KINDS_REQUIRED_FROM}, tags every task; see planning-sprints/resources/templates/sprint-template.md)")
        done
    else
        warnings+=("${plan_date:-undated} plan: ${#bad[@]} task line(s) without a valid kind: tag; the tag is required for plans dated from ${KINDS_REQUIRED_FROM}")
    fi
}

+cannot take effect; `executor.json` records `arm`, `arm_toggles`, `arm_evidence`, `source_commit`,
+`models_used` and `refusal_fallbacks`. The executor never inherits the calling Claude Code session's
+coupling, and its subagent model is pinned to `EVAL_MODEL`.

+`harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh` from `review-prs/record-pairs.tsv` and the `record/cycle-12x-a2a`

    if A["dirty"] or B["dirty"]:
        reasons.append("an arm ran on a prompt tree with uncommitted .claude/ changes")
    # control-arm comparison: each side is one declared arm, and they differ
    control = (len(A["arm_ids"]) == 1 and len(B["arm_ids"]) == 1 and A["arm_ids"] != B["arm_ids"])
    if (not control and A["prompt_trees"] and B["prompt_trees"]

show_help() {
    cat <<EOF
Usage: $SCRIPT_NAME --type prd|sdd|sprint|bug-triage|translation|decisions|map|spike|glossary --file <path>
       [--base-file <path>] [--ledger <path>] [--json]

Validate a Loa planning artifact against its skill-defined structural
contract (grep-based, fail-closed).

Options:
  --type TYPE   Artifact type: prd | sdd | sprint | bug-triage | translation | decisions | map | spike | glossary (required)
  --file PATH   Artifact file to validate (required). For --type translation,
                may also be a directory (validates every *.md under it).
  --base-file PATH
                decisions: the pre-write ledger the append-only check compares
                against (default: the copy at git merge-base origin/main HEAD)
  --ledger PATH prd: the decision ledger the [ASSUMPTION decision] tags cite
                (default: grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml)
  --json        Emit a JSON result object to stdout
  -h, --help    Show this help message

sprint: plans dated from 2026-10-14 end every task line with
  ' · kind: mechanical|judgment|operator' (older plans WARN).

Exit codes:
  0  pass (WARN-level info may still be printed)
  1  fail (exact repair text on stderr)
  2  usage error (missing arguments, unknown type, file not found)
EOF
}

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --type) TYPE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --file) FILE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;

        --ledger) LEDGER_FILE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
